# Why Théia is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Théia** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

Theía has no independent narrative myths; her importance is genealogical and cosmological. Through her, the Titans bequeath light to the Olympian cosmos. Hesiod names Theía as the wife of Hyperion and mother of Hēlios (Sun), Selēnē (Moon), and Eōs (Dawn).  The trio governs the visible heavens; without Theía, there is no source from which these lights can arise.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Théia
- **ASCII form:** theia
- **Meaning:** "Goddess, divine"
- **Domain of influence:** Titaness of Sight
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Θεία
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 238 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Θεία**. On the evidence, it means "Goddess, divine".

Strip **Théia** to *theia* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **e → é** — Acute on the diphthong ει (Θεῖα): the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

None of these marks is decoration. Each one is a fact about how the name was spoken, and each one is checkable against the scholarly record the temple cites.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Théia** lives at [/sites/theia/](/sites/theia/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/theia/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/theia/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/theia/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Théia** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Optics, Imaging & Vision** — Titaness of sight; vision itself.
- **Gems, Jewelry & Luxury Materials** — Gold and clear crystal are her materials; radiance is the jeweler's raw stock.
- **Music, Arts & Performance** — The theater is a seeing-place; her root thea- names the very act of watching.

This is the part of the file that surprises people: a four-thousand-year-old name, mapping cleanly onto twenty-first-century trades. The patterns are not marketing — they are the same myths, read forward.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
